items.title: A mine: cross-section of a machine for extracting water from the pit. Etching by Bénard after L.J. Goussier.
items.date: [between 1700 and 1799] (Wellcome); Minéralogie plate, Diderot/d'Alembert Encyclopédie style (my inference, not stated in the record)
items.depicts: Black-and-white engraved plate (Pl. IV). Top: a large undershot water wheel (water enters from the left at 'A', arrow) on a timber frame with six chain sprockets/pulleys; below ground level a deep timber-lined mine shaft in cross-section, hatched rock on both sides, with long vertical pump rods and chains running down the shaft and a stack of pump barrels on the right side (labels E, F, G, H). Scale bar 'Toises' at lower left. Bottom lettering: 'Minéralogie, Élévation de la Machine pour tirer les Eaux, aux Mines de Pontpéan.' Signed 'Goussier Del.' / 'Benard Fecit'. Shows exactly the problem Savery addressed: water having to be pumped out of a deep mine, here by water-wheel power.

items.title: A mine: cross-section of a machine for extracting water from the pit and three optical diagrams. Etching by T. Jefferys.
items.depicts: Engraved book plate (Plate CLXXX, 'facing page 2123'). Left half, 'Fig. 1. Costar's Engine for raising Water out of MINES': a tall timber frame set against dark rock, with an endless chain of buckets running up a shaft, water spouting out at the top (A) into a trough (W); at the bottom cranks/pump rods (I, K) stand in water (Z) above two pipes (M) going down into the ground. Right half (unrelated): 'Fig. 2. Mirrours' optical ray diagrams and 'Fig. 3. Mnium' (a moss). Signed 'T. Jefferys sculp'. Crop fig1_costar_engine_crop.jpg (1037x3014) keeps only Fig. 1. English, mid-18th c.: the mine-drainage problem.

items.title: A mine: cross-sections of the galleries with miners digging. Etching by R. Bénard after L.J. Goussier.
items.depicts: Engraved plate (Pl. III). Top strip: surface landscape with mountains, a cut-away timber winding house with a large vertical drum, probably a horse gin (Fig. 1), a shed and a wooden launder/bridge (Fig. 2). Below: a cut-away of the ground showing a deep vertical shaft lined with timber cribbing, ladders, and side galleries; small figures of miners hacking at the rock with picks on stepped working faces at the bottom (letters P-V) and one miner in a gallery at left (X); inset vignettes of timbering methods (a-m). Lettering 'Minéralogie, Coupe d'une Mine', 'Goussier Del.', 'Benard Fecit'. Good 'how deep mines are' shot; no water pumping shown explicitly.

items.title: Mijnwerker ('De Bergwercker'), plate 75 of Het Menselyk Bedryf, Jan and Caspar Luyken
items.date: 1694 (Rijksmuseum; first edition of Het Menselyk Bedryf)
items.depicts: Small etching on a sheet with wide margin. Heading 'De Bergwercker.' and motto 'Hoe hoog van waarde, 't Is Stof der Aarden.', number 75. In the picture: a miner in a hooded smock sits resting in the foreground with a cup and bread, beside a wheelbarrow and a pick-axe with lumps of ore; behind him, at a rock face with a cave-like mine entrance, other miners work a large horizontal windlass (hoist) on a timber frame and push barrows; mountains and clouds behind. Below, a six-line Dutch verse ('Al leidt het diep verdeckt voor d'oogen ...'). Exactly period (1694, four years before Savery's patent); shows miners and mine-head hoisting, not water pumping. Picture panel only: approx x 0.09-0.90, y 0.157-0.707.

items.title: The four royall palaces of England viz: St. James's, Kensington, Hampton Court and Windsor (John Bowles) - use the Hampton Court quadrant
items.date: 1723-1733 (Rijksmuseum); the Hampton Court view follows the Kip/Knyff Britannia Illustrata type of c. 1707 (my inference, not in the record)
items.depicts: Large etched sheet with four bird's-eye views; title band 'The Four ROYALL PALACES of ENGLAND viz: St JAMES'S KENSINGTON HAMPTON COURT and WINDSOR ... Dedicated to his most Sacred MAJESTY GEORGE the Second ... John Bowles'. Bottom-left quadrant (crop hampton_court_quadrant_crop.jpg, 3605x2140): 'THE ROYAL PALACE OF HAMPTON COURT' seen from the east: Wren's east front facing the semicircular Great Fountain Garden with box-scroll parterres, fountains and radiating tree avenues, the Long Water/park with deer in the foreground, the Thames with sailing boats at left, the older courts and further walled gardens behind. Caption text includes 'the inward Court was built by K. William & makes a Piazza'. This is the palace as William III rebuilt it, i.e. the setting of Savery's 1698 demonstration (the building, not the event).

items.title: Portrait of Willem III, Prince of Orange, King of England and Stadtholder (Godfried Schalcken)
items.depicts: Oil painting, dark candlelit bust of King William III: long dark curled periwig, pale face looking at the viewer, lace cravat, blue Garter ribbon, ermine-lined mantle over polished steel armour; a tall burning candle at right lights the scene, signed lower left. Painted while he was King of England, within a few years of Savery's 1698 demonstration to him at Hampton Court. Face approx x 0.38-0.57, y 0.16-0.40; candle flame approx x 0.74-0.87, y 0.09-0.30.
